prefLabel: GNI per head at purchasing power parities
altLabel: GNI per capita at PPP | income per head | national income per person | average income
definition: Gross national income (the income earned by an economy's residents, at home and abroad) converted to international dollars with purchasing power parities, which allow for differences in price levels between economies, divided by the resident population. It compares income per head in terms of what it would buy at the same prices in every economy.
scopeNote: What it leaves out: It counts the income of firms and government as well as households, before depreciation; it is an average, so it says nothing about how income is shared; it leaves out unpaid work at home, such as caring, cooking and cleaning, most of it done by women; and price comparisons for some services, such as government health and education, are weak.
definitionSource: data/definitions.csv (approved by the vertical domain expert, 13 Nov 2026)

altLabel: number of people | inhabitants
definition: The number of people living in the economy at mid-year, counting all residents whatever their legal status or citizenship.
scopeNote: What it leaves out: Between censuses the figures are estimates; India's last census was in 2011.

prefLabel: real GDP per hour worked at constant 2021 PPPs
altLabel: labour productivity | output per hour | productivity per hour | GDP per hour worked
definition: GDP at 2021 prices, converted with 2021 purchasing power parities, divided by the total hours worked in the year (persons in work times their average annual hours).
scopeNote: What it leaves out: Hours count paid work and self-employment, not unpaid work at home, such as caring, cooking and cleaning, most of it done by women; total hours are built from Penn World Table estimates; and the output of public services is often measured by what goes in, so output per hour there says little about productivity.

prefLabel: growth in real NNI per head, split into parts
altLabel: what drove income growth | contributions to income growth | decomposition of income growth
definition: The change from the year before in real NNI (net national income) per head, in log points, in five parts that add up exactly: income gap, deflator mix, output per hour worked, hours per worker and workers per person.
scopeNote: What it leaves out: It leaves out unpaid work at home, such as caring, cooking and cleaning, most of it done by women. After the last year with published NNI (2021; United Kingdom 2018), the income gap is estimated, not measured.
